limits: All nine cases were exposed before this method was designed.
Seven of nine reference matches include six UNKNOWN references; always UNKNOWN would match six.
The method retains one clear positive and loses the formerly supported wrong-side failure.
Sixteen new calls reuse paid historical locators and target/crop proposals; cost and latency are incremental, not a cold-start comparison.
Tool mask proximity is a negative warning, not proof of physical contact or separation.
No active acceptance or automatic repair behavior is changed.

limits: All original exposed cases and source views remain; this is not new-source accuracy.
Only pairs with two eligible frozen crop projections enter new inference.
Each eligible pair permits one two-view Spark manipulator locator, at most two spatial SAM requests, and one eight-image Spark mask/contact review.
No manual manipulator anchors, concept retries, favorable substitution or hidden fallback.
Derived target geometry is not a provider response on the full original scene.
Contact, uncertain semantics, incomplete mask coverage or unavailable required evidence cannot authorize a task result.
A far gripper mask is not proof of separation; semantic assessment is fallible and not independent human truth.
Completed missing or unsupported evidence yields UNKNOWN; failed required inference remains unscored.
No production promotion, physical execution or calibrated safety guarantee.
Experimental recorded-source model assessments; no physical action or production promotion.
Original, crop and derived masks are the same physical observation, never extra stable views.
A near foreground proposal can withhold support; far, missing or weak proposals never prove separation.
Released and zero-visible-tool classifications are fallible model assessments, not verified physical absence or execution.
Target and gripper model errors can be correlated; retained hashes prove local consistency, not provider authenticity.
